About Jesse.

I'm a Computer Science undergraduate at the University of Toronto. I build software that connects an interface to a useful system behind it, especially when AI has to deal with changing context and imperfect information.

Recent work has taken me from an AR exhibition guide to campus web agents and a small research prototype about when an agent should trust its memory. I enjoy tracing a system end to end, then making its behavior understandable to the person using it.

In those projects, I keep returning to the same questions: What evidence supports this result? What happens when the input changes? Can the person using the system tell what it did and where it is uncertain?

Outside the project list

As an AI education volunteer in Xinshao, China, I introduced rural learners to computers, classification, and neural networks. When the classroom had no computer for the slides I had prepared, I switched to a simple robot story to explain the idea of machine learning. That experience sharpened how I explain technical work to people with different starting points.

Working with

  • Web: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Fastify
  • AI systems: Python, agent evaluation, evidence handling
  • Devices: Android, Kotlin, camera and media pipelines
